episode_title: Automotive’s New Launchpad: Recycled Batteries, AI Drivers and the Workforce Ahead

real_qa.q: What did General Motors and Cerber Solutions recover from their closed-loop battery recycling pilot?
real_qa.r: General Motors and Cerber Solutions recovered 80 end-of-life battery packs, processed them into black mass, and created over 12 metric tons of new cathode active material. The nickel, cobalt, and manganese were entirely recycled and the material was validated to the same standards as new inputs. Ultium cells made the cells and GM assembled modules at Factory Zero and Spring Hill.
real_qa.requete: General Motors Cerber Solutions battery recycling pilot results

real_qa.q: What new job titles are emerging in battery recycling and circular supply chain roles?
real_qa.r: New job titles emerging include battery lifecycle technician and circular supply chain analyst. Entry-level technicians need high-voltage safety, contamination control, and solid documentation skills. Advanced roles add black mass processing, analytical chemistry, and process controls.
real_qa.requete: battery lifecycle technician job automotive recycling

real_qa.q: What production agreement did Mercedes and Wave sign for AI driver software?
real_qa.r: Mercedes and Wave signed a production agreement to bring Wave AI driver software to future vehicles targeting advanced urban and highway assistance within the next two years. The software is already integrated with Mercedes hardware and map interfaces, and they have done joint demos in three cities.
real_qa.requete: Mercedes Wave AI driver software production agreement

real_qa.q: What are Hyundai's plans for Atlas humanoid robot deployment in automotive manufacturing?
real_qa.r: Hyundai plans 25,000 Atlas deployments across its plants and a U.S. facility to produce 30,000 robots annually. The Boston Dynamics Robotics Metaplant Application Center uses real parts, fixtures, robots, and skilled pilots to generate behavior data as a permanent test bed, with component assembly targeted for 2030.

real_qa.q: Which software platform did Coritura select as its foundational layer for commercial vehicles?
real_qa.r: Coritura, founded by Daimler Truck and Volvo Group, picked AlloyCore as the foundational software layer for its commercial vehicle platform. AlloyCore is developed by Vector and QNX, and this is the platform's first announced design win.
real_qa.requete: Coritura AlloyCore commercial vehicle platform design win

real_qa.q: What cybersecurity regulations are being developed for vehicle software updates and lifecycle management?
real_qa.r: The Unique Cyber and Software Update Group is working on R155 and R156 plus software identification standards for transformed vehicles. R155 focuses on cybersecurity management and R156 on software update management and traceability. ISO and SAE 21434 define lifecycle risk management requirements for road vehicle systems.
